steps.prompt:
You are building the thin MVP of Product Oracle, an AI head-of-product app. Read docs/mvp-app.md in full first (it is the spec), then docs/design.md for context. You own LANE 0 — FOUNDATION only, exactly as docs/mvp-app.md section 'Lanes > Lane 0' defines it; four other lanes start from your branch the moment you finish, so your output is their base.

Build, in this order, committing after each item so partial progress survives:
1. Repo skeleton per 'Layout': api/ (Python 3.12, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, Pydantic v2, uv-managed pyproject), web/ (Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind), docker-compose.yml (postgres:16, api, web), Makefile (up, down, test, lint, migrate, seed, openapi), .github/workflows/ci.yml (ruff, pytest against a Postgres service, next build).
2. api/oracle/{main,config,db,tenancy}.py: settings from env; async engine/session; a tenant-scoped session helper that REFUSES to run a query without a tenant (with a test proving it).
3. ALL SQLAlchemy models from 'Data model' (every table has id uuid pk, tenant_id not null indexed FK, created_at) and migration 0001_initial; `alembic upgrade head` from an empty DB must work.
4. auth/: one admin user (argon2 password hash, session cookie) and API tokens (hashed, Bearer); a seed command creating the tenant, the admin and one API token printed once.
5. Router stubs for EVERY endpoint in 'REST API' returning 501, with Pydantic request/response schemas so the OpenAPI is complete; GET /healthz real (checks DB).
6. `make openapi` writes the OpenAPI JSON and generates web/lib/api/schema.d.ts with openapi-typescript; commit the generated file.
7. The function signature review.service.apply_resolutions(session, document_id, version_id, resolutions) that Lane 1 calls (raise NotImplementedError).
8. web/: a minimal app shell (layout, login page wired to POST /v1/auth/login, empty documents page) so `next build` passes.

Acceptance (from the spec): `make up` starts all three services; migrations apply from empty; login and token auth work (tests); tenant-less queries are refused (test); CI green. Run the tests and the web build yourself before finishing.

Rules: stay inside Lane 0's ownership; do not implement other lanes' logic beyond stubs. No real company, customer or product names anywhere — this repo is public; use the generic fixtures. Keep a short README section 'Run locally'. You have about 2 hours wall clock: if time runs short, finish items 1-5 solidly and list what is left. End by writing a summary of what you built, what is stubbed and anything the next lanes must know to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/lane0-report.md.

You are building the thin MVP of Product Oracle. Read docs/mvp-app.md in full (the spec) and the Lane 0 foundation already in this checkout (models, tenancy helper, auth, router stubs). You own LANE 1 — DOCUMENTS: import, parse, diff (backend), exactly as docs/mvp-app.md 'Lanes > Lane 1' and 'Draft import format' define. Own only api/oracle/docs/, tests/test_parser.py, tests/test_import.py, tests/test_diff.py and tests/fixtures/ (prd_v1.md, prd_v2.md — generic content, e.g. a checkout-redesign PRD; no real company names, the repo is public).

Implement: front-matter + markdown parser (headings level 1-3 must end with {#id}; inline citations [c:id] must exist in front matter; errors -> 422 listing every offending id); POST /v1/documents/{doc}/versions (text/markdown body; creates the document on first import; same content hash -> return existing version 200); sections/citations persisted per the data model; apply `resolutions` by calling review.service.apply_resolutions (implement it if Lane 2's version is not present — keep it in review/service.py minimal and note it in your report); locked_section_changed warning when a section approved in the previous version changes; GET versions list/read/markdown; GET /v1/documents/{doc}/diff?from=&to= with section-level added/removed/changed/moved and word-level changes inside changed sections.

Acceptance: every check in the Lane 1 'Accept' line, as pytest tests against Postgres. Do not touch migrations or models (Lane 0 owns them); if you truly need a column, stop and write it in your report instead. Run the full test suite before finishing. Write your summary to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/lane1-report.md.

You are building the thin MVP of Product Oracle. Read docs/mvp-app.md in full (the spec) and the Lane 0 foundation already in this checkout. You own LANE 2 — REVIEW AND FEEDBACK (backend), exactly as docs/mvp-app.md 'Lanes > Lane 2' defines. Own only api/oracle/review/ and its tests (tests/test_review*.py).

Implement: inline comments with a W3C TextQuoteSelector anchor {exact, prefix, suffix} on a version + section_key, replies, resolve (POST/GET .../versions/{n}/comments, POST /v1/comments/{id}/replies, PATCH /v1/comments/{id}); section verdicts PUT .../versions/{n}/sections/{key}/review (approved / changes_requested / rejected + note; history kept, latest wins); feedback items created on every comment and non-approved verdict, a later verdict on the same section superseding the earlier item; GET /v1/documents/{doc}/feedback?status=&version=; PATCH /v1/feedback/{id}; GET .../versions/{n}/feedback-package (version markdown, open items, locked = approved section ids); GET .../versions/{n}/resolution-report (every item raised on earlier versions with its outcome); POST .../versions/{n}/approve (document -> approved, version approved_at); review.service.apply_resolutions(...) fully implemented (Lane 1 calls it on import). Write audit_events for every mutation.

To test without Lane 1, insert documents/versions/sections directly in fixtures. Do not touch migrations or models; if you need a column, write it in your report. Acceptance: every check in the Lane 2 'Accept' line as pytest tests. Write your summary to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/lane2-report.md.

You are building the thin MVP of Product Oracle. Read docs/mvp-app.md in full (the spec) and the Lane 0 foundation already in this checkout. You own LANE 3 — EXPORT AND AGENT BRIDGE, exactly as docs/mvp-app.md 'Lanes > Lane 3' defines. Own only api/oracle/export/, api/oracle/cli/, export tests, and the api Dockerfile's system dependencies for PDF.

Implement: GET .../versions/{n}/export?format=html|pdf|md — HTML via a Jinja2 template (templates/prd.html.j2 + static/prd.css: clean, print-friendly, all sections in order, citations rendered as numbered footnotes with links and excerpts, a version banner with number, status and date); PDF with WeasyPrint from the same HTML; md = the stored markdown with a banner comment. The `oracle` CLI (api/oracle/cli/oracle_cli.py, installed as a console script): `oracle push <draft.md> [--doc slug]` POSTs to the import endpoint with the API token from ORACLE_API_TOKEN and ORACLE_URL and prints the version number and warnings; `oracle pull <doc> --version N [--out dir]` writes the feedback package (markdown, open items JSON, locked ids) to disk.

To test without Lanes 1 and 2, build versions directly in fixtures and mock HTTP for the CLI. Do not touch migrations or models. Acceptance: every check in the Lane 3 'Accept' line as pytest tests (the PDF test asserts a valid PDF with the expected page text). Write your summary to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/lane3-report.md.

You are building the thin MVP of Product Oracle. Read docs/mvp-app.md in full (the spec) and the Lane 0 foundation in this checkout, especially web/ and the generated web/lib/api/schema.d.ts. You own LANE 4 — WEB UI, exactly as docs/mvp-app.md 'Lanes > Lane 4' defines. Own only web/ (never edit the generated schema file).

Build with Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind, typed against schema.d.ts through a small fetch client (lib/api/client.ts) with a mock mode (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCKS=1) backed by realistic generic fixtures, because the backend lanes are being built in parallel: login; documents list; version view (sections in order, citation chips showing source, title and excerpt on hover/click); select text -> comment popover -> comment saved with a TextQuoteSelector {exact, prefix, suffix} and re-anchored on reload; per-section verdict bar (approve / request changes / reject + note) with locked indication; feedback panel with status/version filters; version switcher; diff view (section-level badges + word-level highlights); approve and export (HTML/PDF/MD) buttons. Product feel: a calm, professional review workspace — clear hierarchy, readable typography, keyboard-friendly, works at laptop width; no gratuitous colour.

Add Playwright tests running in mock mode for: login, open a version, add an anchored comment that survives reload, set a verdict, switch versions, open the diff. `next build` and the Playwright suite must pass. No real company or customer names (public repo). Write your summary, including what still runs on mocks, to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/lane4-report.md.
